Bat-wing finial spires crowned in tarnished silver, each tip clutching a ruby orb, rise from the castle parapets against a perpetual blood-moon sky.
Drăculești dragon-cross heraldry embossed in hammered gold across load-bearing keystones, the serpent devouring its own tail around a crimson Wallachian cross.
Sapphire-stained-glass rose-windows filtering moonlight into cold cobalt pools across marble floors, each petal panel depicting a fallen Belmont ancestor mid-battle.
Gold-leafed crockets spiraling up every nave pilaster, thick with acanthus-and-bone motifs, the gilding deliberately tarnished at edges to suggest centuries of dark occupation.
Wrought-iron bat-and-wyvern gates, each bar twisted into serpentine coils terminating in spread-winged bat silhouettes, flanked by stone wyverns with onyx inlaid eyes.
Scarlet-velvet banner-drops cascading forty feet from ribbed vaulted ceilings, embroidered in gold thread with the Belmont whip-crest mirrored against Dracula's dragon seal.
Carved-marble gargoyle balustrades lining every interior gallery, each creature rendered mid-shriek with articulated stone wings brushing the adjacent column in art-nouveau sinuous grace.
Vine-and-skull tracery climbing the full height of every pointed arch, the skeletal motif woven seamlessly into flowering nightshade vines across pale limestone panels.
Fallen-angel statuary positioned at each corridor intersection, white Carrara marble wings deliberately fractured, faces tilted downward in expressions of exquisite grief and submission.
Chandelier-windows glowing with interior amber candlelight visible from the courtyard, their leaded ironwork shaped as interlocking bat-wing medallions suspended between lancet arch ribs.
Gothic-arched doorways with carved saints rendered in Ayami Kojima's elongated proportions, robes dissolving at hemlines into curling smoke and thorned-rose relief sculpture.
Dragon-head water-spouts projecting from each tower cornice, bronze mouths open in eternal silent roars, verdigris staining the ashlar below in long emerald tears.
Bronze-and-gold cornice trim running the full castle perimeter, alternating skull-boss and lotus-blossom motifs cast in high relief against a band of midnight-blue enamel.
Opulent gilt-frame ornament surrounding every interior mirror, the frames cast as entwined serpents and crescent moons, the glass tinted slightly amber — nothing reflects truly.
Ribbed stone vaulting painted in deep Prussian blue between each rib, constellations picked out in gold leaf forming the Drăculești zodiac across the great hall ceiling.
Wrought-iron candelabra brackets shaped as upward-reaching skeletal hands, each finger terminating in a beeswax candle socket, bolted between every stained-glass lancet window.
Organ-pipe clusters repurposed as decorative wall columns in the music chamber, their burnished tin surfaces engraved with bat silhouettes and Order of Ecclesia glyphs.
Mosaic tile floors depicting the eternal damnation cycle in Byzantine tesserae — gold, crimson, and bone-white chips arranged in concentric mandala patterns below the throne dais.
Bloodlines-era iron portcullis framing, its vertical bars crowned with fleur-de-lis tips dipped in red enamel, horizontal rails forged into continuous leaping-wolf relief friezes.
Travertine column capitals carved as Lords of Shadow grotesque faces, each unique, mouths open and spilling carved stone tongues that curl into supporting corbel brackets.
Symphony-of-the-Night inverted-castle logic expressed architecturally: stalactite-pendant bosses of carved granite hang from what appears simultaneously as floor and ceiling in recursive ornament.
Order of Ecclesia glyph-circles inlaid in electrum across chapel antechamber thresholds, the Dominus and Volaticus symbols interlocking within a wreathing border of carved hemlock.
Carved-limestone lancet window jambs featuring continuous narrative bas-relief — Shanoa's absorption glyphs, Alucard's sword, and Richter's whip-arc rendered in spiraling sequential panels.
Midnight-blue ceramic tile dados lining lower corridor walls, each tile hand-painted with a unique moth-and-moonflower motif echoing Ayami Kojima's nocturnal illustration palette.
Copper-roofed turret caps oxidized to deep verdigris, each roof ridge terminated with a cast-bronze bat finial whose wingspan spans the full turret diameter in spread glory.
Bat-wing finial spires crown each tower turret, their obsidian iron frameworks spread wide like a vampiric wingspan, gilded along every vein with tarnished gold leaf catching candlelight from below.

Drăculești dragon-cross heraldry embossed in hammered bronze dominates the great hall tympanum — coiled wyvern clutching an inverted crucifix, scales picked out in verdigris and blood-crimson enamel inlay.

Sapphire rose-windows flood the nave in cobalt and violet spectral light, each petal-lancet filled with leaded glass depicting fallen seraphim descending through storm clouds toward a moonlit castle keep.

Wrought-iron bat-and-wyvern gates bracket the portcullis arch, twin serpentine creatures intertwined at the crown, their hollow eye-sockets set with glowing amber glass that pulses faint as dying embers.

Vine-and-skull tracery climbs every pillar shaft — marble morning-glory tendrils curling between grinning death's-heads, the organic growth frozen mid-bloom as though the castle itself breathes and slowly consumes its own stone.
